sector_model: software/AI platform: EV/sales, P/E GAAP, FCF yield after SBC, net cash, dilution
thesis: Palantir (Nasdaq: PLTR) is growing extremely fast: Q3 2026 revenue 2,313.4M (+96%), government +81%, commercial +113%, GAAP operating income 1,084.8M (47% margin), GAAP net income attributable 1,128.0M, FY26 revenue guide 8.53B and adjusted FCF 4.8-5.0B. Balance sheet 10.56B cash and securities, no borrowings. TTM revenue 7,288M, TTM FCF 4,054M (capex only 43M), SBC TTM 982M. At 171.58 (2026-11-12 close) market cap about 413B, EV about 403B: 55x TTM sales, 47x FY26 guided sales, 113x TTM GAAP earnings, FCF yield 0.98% (0.74% after SBC). Business quality is evidently high; the price already assumes growth near current rates for many years. No mispricing demonstrated; this is a strong business at a demanding price.
counterthesis: At about 55x TTM sales and about 1% FCF yield the price requires sustained 50%+ growth; a deceleration or any government budget shift would compress the multiple sharply (52-week range 106.37-212.94, now 19% below high; that is not evidence of cheapness). GAAP net income is flattered by a tax provision of only about 1% of pretax income and by interest income; SBC is 13% of 9M revenue and diluted shares exceed basic shares by about 7%. Customer I is 27% of receivables; government is about half of revenue. Peer comparison, 10-K risk factors, Item 4 and auditor matters unread; quotes from two publishers only.
invalidation: Quality thesis fails if quarterly revenue growth falls below about 40%, GAAP operating margin falls below 30%, or SBC dilution accelerates. Valuation case would need a price near 10-15x guided sales or FCF yield after SBC above 4%, none close to current.
